# Backtests and strategies

<!-- Generated by scripts/core_docs.py; edit the source of truth and regenerate. -->

Authors declare strategy defaults with backtest; the host constructs and executes Backtest, and Strategy defines initialization and bar-by-bar trading logic.

[Usage guide](../quickstart.md) · [Compatibility and internal entries](classification.md)

<a id="openbacktesting-backtest"></a>

## Backtest

Qualified object: `openbacktesting.Backtest`

```python
openbacktesting.Backtest(data: 'pd.DataFrame', strategy: 'type[Strategy]', *, cash: 'float' = 10000, spread: 'float' = 0.0, commission: 'float | tuple[float, float] | Commission | Callable[[float, float], float]' = 0.0, risk_free_rate: 'float' = 0.0, default_order_size: 'DefaultOrderSize | None' = None, margin: 'float' = 1.0, execution_timing='next_open', instrument=None, slippage=None, allow_short=True, max_gross_exposure=None, hedging=False, exclusive_orders=False, end_policy='mark_to_market', indicator_cache_bytes=67108864, context: 'DataContext | None' = None, plotting: 'bool' = True, plotting_limits: 'PlottingLimits | None' = None, _collection: 'CollectionPolicy' = CollectionPolicy(portfolio=True, logs=True, plotting=True))
```

Store single-asset historical market data, strategy, and linear margin-account configuration.

data OHLC must contain finite positive prices, with an ordered unique index. instrument specifies quantity steps and an optional price grid.
cash is the initial balance; margin is the notional margin fraction; hedging controls retention of two-sided lots.
commission may be a rate, (fixed fee, rate), Commission, or pure fee function, charged once per actual execution.
spread and slippage apply to every buy/sell execution; slippage never permits orders to cross their limits.
execution_timing supports next_open or same_close; end_policy supports mark_to_market or close_at_last_close.
allow_short controls new short positions; max_gross_exposure caps gross notional/equity; valid reductions are always allowed.
exclusive_orders cancels previous entries and submits exits for existing lots when a new ordinary order is submitted.
context is optional; when provided, it requires a timezone-aware index and converts display timezone on a copy; strategies can read self.timeframe.
risk_free_rate is an annualized fraction affecting statistics only; default_order_size supplies the request budget when qty is omitted.
Low-level construction does not automatically merge @backtest settings; runtime handles declaration adoption.
No legacy size-fraction inference, price scaling, cross-currency trading, volume-based partial fills, or live execution.

Source: `src/openbacktesting/simulation/core.py`。

<a id="openbacktesting-backtest-optimize"></a>

### optimize

Qualified object: `openbacktesting.Backtest.optimize`

```python
openbacktesting.Backtest.optimize(self, *, maximize: 'str | Callable[[pd.Series], float]' = 'SQN', method: 'str' = 'grid', max_tries: 'float | None' = None, constraint: 'Callable[[dict], bool] | None' = None, return_heatmap: 'bool' = False, return_optimization: 'bool' = False, random_state: 'int | None' = None, **kwargs) -> 'pd.Series | tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series] | tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series, dict]'
```

Search strategy-parameter combinations and select results by a specified statistic or scoring function.


Optimize strategy parameters to an optimal combination.
Returns result `pd.Series` of the best run.

`maximize` is a string key from the
`openbacktesting.engine.Backtest.run`-returned results series,
or a function that accepts this series object and returns a number;
the higher the better. By default, the method maximizes
Van Tharp's [System Quality Number](https://altpower.app/?q=System+Quality+Number).

`method` is the optimization method. Currently two methods are supported:

* `"grid"` which does an exhaustive (or randomized) search over the
  cartesian product of parameter combinations, and
* `"sambo"` which finds close-to-optimal strategy parameters using
  [model-based optimization], making at most `max_tries` evaluations.

[model-based optimization]: https://sambo-optimization.github.io

`max_tries` is the maximal number of strategy runs to perform.
If `method="grid"`, this results in randomized grid search.
If `max_tries` is a floating value between (0, 1], this sets the
number of runs to approximately that fraction of full grid space.
Alternatively, if integer, it denotes the absolute maximum number
of evaluations. If unspecified (default), grid search is exhaustive,
whereas for `method="sambo"`, `max_tries` is set to 200.

`constraint` is a function that accepts a dict-like object of
parameters (with values) and returns `True` when the combination
is admissible to test with. By default, any parameters combination
is considered admissible.

If `return_heatmap` is `True`, besides returning the result
series, an additional `pd.Series` is returned with a multiindex
of all admissible parameter combinations, which can be further
inspected as a table of parameter combinations and objective values.

If `return_optimization` is True and `method = 'sambo'`,
in addition to result series (and maybe heatmap), return raw
[`scipy.optimize.OptimizeResult`][OptimizeResult] for further
inspection by the caller.

[OptimizeResult]: https://sambo-optimization.github.io/doc/sambo/#sambo.OptimizeResult
[SAMBO]: https://sambo-optimization.github.io

If you want reproducible optimization results, set `random_state`
to a fixed integer random seed.

Additional keyword arguments represent strategy arguments with
list-like collections of possible values. For example, the following
code finds and returns the "best" of the 7 admissible (of the
9 possible) parameter combinations:

    best_stats = backtest.optimize(sma1=[5, 10, 15], sma2=[10, 20, 40],
                                   constraint=lambda p: p.sma1 < p.sma2)

Source: `src/openbacktesting/simulation/core.py`。

<a id="openbacktesting-backtest-run"></a>

### run

Qualified object: `openbacktesting.Backtest.run`

```python
openbacktesting.Backtest.run(self, **kwargs) -> 'pd.Series'
```

Backtest strategy parameters and return a statistics Series, plain-value ledger tables, and an optional diagnostic strategy.

Public statistics keys:
Start, End, Duration, Exposure Time [%]
Equity Final [$], Equity Peak [$], Return [%], Buy & Hold Return [%]
Return (Ann.) [%], Volatility (Ann.) [%], CAGR [%], Sharpe Ratio
Sortino Ratio, Calmar Ratio, Alpha [%], Beta
Max. Drawdown [%], Avg. Drawdown [%], Max. Drawdown Duration, Avg. Drawdown Duration
# Trades, Win Rate [%], Best Trade [%], Worst Trade [%]
Avg. Trade [%], Max. Trade Duration, Avg. Trade Duration, Profit Factor
Expectancy [%], SQN, Kelly Criterion, Commissions [$]
# Closed Lots, _strategy, _equity_curve, _trades
_orders, _order_sizing, _order_events, _fills, _trade_allocations
_positions, _account_curve, _final_account, _open_trades

Order and fill events are not gated by indicator NaN; next runs on every bar starting with the first.
Retain account and gross exposure on each normal bar; record terminal handling in a separate terminal snapshot.
Result attrs contain trading-policy version, configuration, and input snapshots; _strategy is not required to reconstruct trading facts.

Source: `src/openbacktesting/simulation/core.py`。

<a id="openbacktesting-strategy"></a>

## Strategy

Qualified object: `openbacktesting.Strategy`

```python
openbacktesting.Strategy(broker, data, params)
```

Strategy base class: Register indicators in init and place orders from currently visible history in next.


A trading strategy base class. Extend this class and
override methods
`openbacktesting.engine.Strategy.init` and
`openbacktesting.engine.Strategy.next` to define
your own strategy.

Source: `src/openbacktesting/strategy/base.py`。

<a id="openbacktesting-strategy-ind"></a>

### ind

Qualified object: `openbacktesting.Strategy.ind`

```python
openbacktesting.Strategy.ind(self, func: 'Callable', *args, name=None, **kwargs) -> 'IndicatorHandle'
```

Compute custom indicators in bulk during initialization and return read-only handles read through the backtest cursor.

Register the same function with different parameters or reuse it across strategies. Each registration executes the
function without sharing a custom-computation cache; prefer ``self.ta`` for built-in formulas.
Functions receive complete history in init; authors must ensure computations depend only on current and past data.

Args:
    func: Computation function returning one- or two-dimensional array-like output with time-axis length equal to market data.
        Series/DataFrame indices must exactly match market data; arrays align by position.
    *args: Positional arguments passed unchanged to the computation function.
    name: Display name or sequence of multi-output channel names, with length equal to the channel count.
        Defaults to the function and arguments; format fields in names are filled from computation arguments.
    **kwargs: Keyword arguments passed unchanged to the computation function.

Returns:
    Read-only IndicatorHandle. Access named channels with ``result['middle']``;
    ``np.asarray()``, ``.s``, and ``.df`` return prefix snapshots at read time.

Raises:
    IndicatorError: Registration outside init, changed market-data source, or misaligned pandas index.
    TypeError: name is not a string or string sequence.
    ValueError: Output shape, length, or channel-name count does not match.
    RuntimeError: User-function computation failed, with the original exception retained as cause.

Note:
    ready defaults to all True; valid depends on finite values. next runs on every bar starting with the first;
    authors must check history length and valid for the channels they use. Invalid indicators do not suppress callbacks.
    More complex output masks are not public parameters of this entry point.

Source: `src/openbacktesting/strategy/base.py`。

### buy

Qualified object: `openbacktesting.Strategy.buy`

```python
openbacktesting.Strategy.buy(self, *, qty: 'float' = <_Unset.VALUE: 'omitted'>, amount: 'float' = <_Unset.VALUE: 'omitted'>, percent: 'float' = <_Unset.VALUE: 'omitted'>, limit: 'float | None' = None, stop: 'float | None' = None, sl: 'float | None' = None, tp: 'float | None' = None, tag: '_JsonValue' = None, reduce_only: 'bool' = False, expires_at: '_Expiry | None' = None, valid_bars: 'int | None' = None) -> 'Order'
```

Omitting all choices uses the default quantity. Amount is a single-currency notional budget excluding fees;
convert and freeze it using Close at request time, with rejection still possible at execution. Reduce-only requires explicit qty.

<a id="openbacktesting-strategy-data"></a>

### data

Qualified object: `openbacktesting.Strategy.data`

```python
openbacktesting.Strategy.data(self) -> '_Data'
```

Currently visible original market-data entry point; full history in init and only the current prefix in next.


Price data, roughly as passed into
`openbacktesting.engine.Backtest.__init__`,
but with two significant exceptions:

* `data` is _not_ a DataFrame, but a custom structure
  that serves customized numpy arrays for reasons of performance
  and convenience. Besides OHLCV columns, `.index` and length,
  it offers `.pip` property, the smallest price unit of change.
* Within `openbacktesting.engine.Strategy.init`, `data` arrays
  are available in full length, as passed into
  `openbacktesting.engine.Backtest.__init__`
  (for precomputing indicators and such). However, within
  `openbacktesting.engine.Strategy.next`, `data` arrays are
  only as long as the current iteration, simulating gradual
  price point revelation. In each call of
  `openbacktesting.engine.Strategy.next` (iteratively called by
  `openbacktesting.engine.Backtest` internally),
  the last array value (e.g. `data.Close[-1]`)
  is always the **most recent** value.
* If you need data arrays (e.g. `data.Close`) to be indexed
  **Pandas series**, you can call their `.s` accessor
  (e.g. `data.Close.s`). If you need the whole of data
  as a **DataFrame**, use `.df` accessor (i.e. `data.df`).

Source: `src/openbacktesting/strategy/base.py`。

<a id="openbacktesting-strategy-next"></a>

### next

Qualified object: `openbacktesting.Strategy.next`

```python
openbacktesting.Strategy.next(self)
```

Per-bar strategy callback, starting at input bar 0 and called once for each normally reached bar.

Called even with insufficient or invalid indicator history; check length before [-2] and valid before consuming indicators.
bar_index/bar_state represent the current input position and frozen first/last state.


Main strategy runtime method, called as each new
`openbacktesting.engine.Strategy.data`
instance (row; full candlestick bar) becomes available.
This is the main method where strategy decisions
upon data precomputed in `openbacktesting.engine.Strategy.init`
take place.

If you extend composable strategies from `openbacktesting.lib`,
make sure to call:

    super().next()

Source: `src/openbacktesting/strategy/base.py`。

<a id="openbacktesting-strategy-order-target-quantity"></a>

### order_target_quantity

Qualified object: `openbacktesting.Strategy.order_target_quantity`

```python
openbacktesting.Strategy.order_target_quantity(self, *, target: 'float', limit: 'float | None' = None, stop: 'float | None' = None, sl: 'float | None' = None, tp: 'float | None' = None, tag: '_JsonValue' = None, reduce_only: 'bool' = False, expires_at: '_Expiry | None' = None, valid_bars: 'int | None' = None) -> 'Order | None'
```

Generate a difference order from the actual net position; always validate conditions and reuse identical active targets.

target is the target asset quantity; return None when no order is needed. Only netting mode is supported.
All arguments must be supplied by name; limit/stop/sl/tp are absolute prices.
Validate prices, expiration, and tags even with no difference; do not invent a buy/sell direction to check protection relationships.

Source: `src/openbacktesting/strategy/base.py`。

<a id="openbacktesting-backtest-declaration"></a>

## backtest

Qualified object: `openbacktesting.backtest`

```python
openbacktesting.backtest(*, cash: float = 10000, spread: float = 0.0, commission_type: openbacktesting.simulation.config.CommissionType = <CommissionType.PERCENT: 'percent'>, commission_value: float = 0.0, risk_free_rate: float = 0.0, default_qty_type: openbacktesting.simulation.config.QuantityType = <QuantityType.FIXED: 'fixed'>, default_qty_value: float | None = None, margin: float = 1.0, execution_timing: openbacktesting.simulation.config.ExecutionTiming = <ExecutionTiming.NEXT_OPEN: 'next_open'>, slippage_type: openbacktesting.simulation.config.SlippageType = <SlippageType.BPS: 'bps'>, slippage_value: float = 0.0, allow_short: bool = True, max_gross_exposure: float | None = None, hedging: bool = False, exclusive_orders: bool = False, end_policy: openbacktesting.simulation.config.EndPolicy = <EndPolicy.MARK_TO_MARKET: 'mark_to_market'>) -> collections.abc.Callable[[type[~_S]], type[~_S]]
```

Attach default backtest settings to a concrete strategy class; the host supplies actual market data and execution.

Accept only primitive values and corresponding enum members; fixed options reject bare strings and other enums.
Only the decorator form with parentheses is supported. Algorithm parameters still use inputs; instrument,
timeframe, and resource options are not accepted. The framework constructs the configuration model and returns the original strategy class.

Args:
    cash: Positive finite initial account balance.
    spread: Fractional spread for every buy/sell execution, in [0,1).
    commission_type: One commission type: PERCENT, CASH_PER_ORDER, or CASH_PER_CONTRACT.
    commission_value: PERCENT uses percentage points in [-10,10); 0.2 means 0.2%, and negative values are rebates;
        other types use nonnegative amounts, charged per actual Fill or actual asset unit respectively.
    risk_free_rate: Annualized fraction in (-1,1), used only for statistics without accruing account interest.
    default_qty_type: FIXED means fixed quantity; PERCENT_OF_EQUITY means equity percentage.
    default_qty_value: None disables default sizing; FIXED is positive, and equity percentage is in (0,100].
        Only ordinary buy/sell orders omitting qty use Close and equity at request time to budget, round toward zero, and freeze quantity.
    margin: Margin fraction in (0,1], without amplifying the default quantity budget.
    execution_timing: NEXT_OPEN or SAME_CLOSE; the latter handles only new unconditional market orders from next.
    slippage_type: FIXED means a fixed price distance; BPS means basis points.
    slippage_value: Nonnegative slippage value; zero means no slippage.
    allow_short: Whether new short positions are allowed; strictly bool.
    max_gross_exposure: None or a positive cap on gross notional/equity.
    hedging: Whether to retain two-sided lots; strictly bool.
    exclusive_orders: Whether a new ordinary entry cancels prior entries and submits exits for existing positions; strictly bool.
    end_policy: MARK_TO_MARKET retains marked positions; CLOSE_AT_LAST_CLOSE liquidates actual positions.

Raises:
    TypeError: Invalid types, enums, fields, or decorator targets.
    ValueError: Out-of-range numbers or duplicate declarations on the same strategy.

Source: `src/openbacktesting/strategy/declaration.py`。
